correctness.rationale: Every horizontal and vertical color is a 2n-edge perfect matching in the 4n-vertex prism. For every connecting W, summing component deficits over n+1 colors gives n|W|>=(n+1)(2n-1), whence |W|>=2n+1. The explicit 2n+1-edge set gives a double-star spanning tree upon contracting the vertical color, and for each horizontal color makes layer1 connected, layer0 at most two components, and bridges both components to layer1; valid for all n>=2 and all independently chosen 1-factorizations. Replayed verifier confirms finite cases, not relied on for the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The 2026 paper proves exact wld(K_mn)=n and product lower bounds for two complete-bipartite factors K_{m,n} and K_{s,t}, requiring s>=2. K_2=K_{1,1} falls outside; a component lower bound alone cannot imply an exact result without an upper witness. Its product coloring uses the same factor coloring in both copies, whereas arbitrary independent layer factorizations are permitted here.

value.rationale: The invariant is explicitly motivated by a 2026 investigation of wild numbers under graph Cartesian products, which previously obtained only broad lower bounds for two large factors. The new two-star/two-bridge witness attains the component lower bound for the natural K_nn prism infinite family even when the layer 1-factorizations differ. This is a nontrivial sharpness mechanism, not a renamed bound or a fixed-size computation, and delineates its limits.
